messages.subject: Populating a matrix
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to populate a matrix for based on initial conditions for the Ricker equation and then plot it. I'm getting errors about the length of the of objects in the function. Apologies in advance if I did not format this correctly.

Ricker_eq = function(N_t, K, R){ #function with default values of K and r
  Ricker = N_t*exp(r*(1-N_t/K))
  #Ricker equation
  return(Ricker)
  #returns equation value
}

tf=100 #final time
t=1 #starting at time 1
k=100
n0=5 #initial value

bifr <- seq(1.5,3.6, by = 0.1) #r for the bifurcation section
bifrlength <- length(bifr) #length used for the number of rows in the matrix
bifn <- matrix(NA, nrow = tf, ncol = bifrlength)
colnames(bifn) <- bifr #naming columns with value of r
rownames(bifn) <- 1:tf #naming rows with time point
bifn[1,] = n0
for(x in 1:(tf-1)){ #loop through time
  bifn[x+1,] = Ricker_eq(bifn[x,] ,k ,bifr) #using Ricker_eq model
}
head(bifn)
#plot r vs n output at final time


#final code to plot the matrix on one plot
matplot(bifr,bifn[,1:100], type='l', xlab="Time", ylab= "Population size") #plot matrix

#errors-----------
1: In r * (1 - N_t/K) :
  longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length
2: In r * (1 - N_t/K) :
  longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length
3: In r * (1 - N_t/K) :
  longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length
etc.

 #matplot(bifr,bifn[,1:100], type='l', xlab="Time", ylab= "Population size") #plot matrix
#Error in bifn[, 1:100] : subscript out of bounds

messages.author: f8f554f3c8aec296
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Populating a matrix
parts:
It's unclear to me what you are trying to plot. If you are really trying to plot the r vs N at the final time, replace the last line with:
plot(bifr,bifn[,tf], type='l',  xlab="growth rate (R)", ylab= "Population size") # you don't need matplot to just plot N at final time

The first few errors are caused, I think, by a typo in `Ricker_eq`. On the first line of the function replacing `exp(r*(` with `exp(R * (` fixes this.

- Jaime

messages.author: f8f554f3c8aec296
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Populating a matrix
parts:
Nice.

Assuming you mean 'r vs N' and using all the data you have from time 1 to 100, note that `matplot` plots the columns of one matrix against the cols of the other. It'll treat a vector as a one-column matrix, so this will work (by transposing `bifn` to have one row for every value of r in `bifr`):

matplot(bifr, t(bifn), type='l', xlab="rate (R)", ylab= "Population size") #plot matrix
On Mon, Jan 23, 2017 at 4:08 PM, <da.hern...@gmail.com> wrote:

Thank you! The typo in the Ricker function was causing the errors.

With regards to the plot: I am trying to the value of r vs. N at every single time point

-David
